Lozano -- "A pipeline fire that burned in a Houston suburb for four days finally went out Thursday as authorities announced a criminal investigation into the blaze that had roared into a towering flame, forcing neighborhoods to evacuate and melting parts of nearby cars. Before the fire fully stopped Thursday evening, officials announced that human remains were found in an SUV that had been next to the flame since the explosion happened Monday. Investigators say the fire began after the driver of that car went through a fence alongside a Walmart parking lot and struck an above-ground valve. Officials in Deer Park, where the explosion occurred, described the crash as an accident, and said police and local FBI agents have not found evidence of a coordinated or terrorist attack. "This has developed into a criminal investigation and will be actively ongoing until more information is available," the city said in a statement late Thursday. As authorities worked to identify who had driven the vehicle, residents who were forced to flee the towering blaze returned to assess the damage on Thursday. They found mailboxes and vehicles partially melted by the intense heat, a neighborhood park charred and destroyed and fences burned to the ground. "Devastated, upset, scared. We don't know what we're going to do now," said Diane Hutto , 51, after finding her home severely damaged by water that firefighters poured on it to keep it from catching fire. Hutto's home is located only a few hundred feet from the pipeline. Before the fire went out, its reduced size meant police finally had access to the area around the pipeline. Investigators removed the white SUV and towed it away Thursday morning. While medical examiners with Harris County were processing the vehicle, they recovered and removed human remains found inside, Deer Park officials said in a statement. Officials say the underground pipeline, which runs under high-voltage power lines in a grassy corridor between the Walmart and a residential neighborhood, was damaged when the SUV driver left the store's parking lot, entered the wide grassy area and went through a fence surrounding the valve equipment. But authorities have offered few details on what caused the vehicle to crash through the fence and hit the pipeline valve. Energy Transfer, the Dallas-based company that owns the pipeline, on Wednesday called it an accident. Deer Park officials said preliminary investigations by police and FBI agents found no evidence of a terrorist attack. The pipeline is a 20-inch-wide conduit that runs for miles through the Houston area. It carries natural gas liquids through Deer Park and La Porte, both of which are southeast of Houston. nearly 1,000 homes at one point and ordered people in nearby schools to shelter in place. name: Gene Karpinski, LCV President
subject: Thank You
body:
A Special Announcement from LCV President Gene Karpinski

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTE1MzE3MDQS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjA2MDQxNzQyNwS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | Dear Peter,
---
| | Earlier this week, I announced that after more than 18 years as president of the League of Conservation Voters (LCV) — and another dozen years on LCV’s Board before that — I plan to step down next year.
---
| | I’m very proud of all that LCV has accomplished, and I’m immensely grateful for the generosity of supporters like you who have fueled our organizations’ ability to secure a safer, healthier, and more just climate future and democracy for all.
---
| | During this time, together we:
---
| |
* Helped pass and enact **the biggest climate action investment in U.S. history,** the Inflation Reduction Act, by launching an 18-month nationwide advocacy campaign.
* Launched the Clean Energy for All campaign, alongside our 30+ state affiliates, to secure **clean energy commitments from municipalities and states** across the nation. Today over 40% of people in the U.S. live in places committed to 100% clean energy — more than triple the percentage when we started.
* Launched the Clean Buses for Healthy Niños campaign, led by our Chispa program, which has secured **$5 billion in federal funding for clean school buses,** doubling the number of electric school buses across the U.S. and protecting children’s health.
* Helped elect and re-elect **thousands of pro-climate, pro-democracy candidates** up and down the ballot through the independent expenditure campaigns of LCV Victory Fund and its affiliated entities.
* Raised tens of millions of dollars in support of **climate and democracy champions** through our GiveGreen program.
* Pushed the Biden-Harris administration to finalize a record number of **executive actions to cut pollution and protect public lands,** thanks to our grassroots organizing, advocacy, and accountability work.
* Helped our 30+ state affiliates in the Conservation Voters Movement push for the passage of an unprecedented number of **state-level policies** that curb climate change and strengthen our democracy.

---
| | These successes were preceded by historic investments, particularly over the last eight years, to help elect pro-climate, pro-democracy candidates at the national, state, and local levels — none of which would have been possible without supporters like you.
---
| | Thanks to you, we’ve built a much more powerful environmental movement, strengthened partnerships with labor, environmental justice, and democracy allies, and made climate action a priority issue for the public, the media, and elected leaders.
---
| | I am deeply appreciative of every single person who is and has been a part of our work. You’ve helped make this journey so much fun, so rewarding, and so successful, and I am proud of all that we’ve accomplished together.
---
| | **I’m also keenly aware that we have so much more to do to secure our democracy and protect our planet.** Although I have no specific plans for my future after LCV, I know I’ll remain in the fight to protect our planet and our democracy. I’m counting on you — as are future generations — to do the same.
---
| | With just weeks to go until the election, we need to keep our eyes on the prize and win in November, and then continue to make more progress to protect our planet and our democracy in 2025 and beyond. [**Please consider supporting — or increasing your support for — our work at this critical time.**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | Thank you for all you’ve done and all you will continue to do to ensure a safe, livable, and just future for all.
---
| | Cheers and onward,
---
| | Gene Karpinski, _LCV President_
---
